questions.prompt: How is "overdue" defined in the library tracker, and how should an overdue list be built on top of it? Give the rule and say whether anything is stored, how the reference getOverdueBooks reuses the rule and why it needs both no null guard and an explicit tie-break, why an overdue flag must not be persisted, and the clock problem the review found in the CLI's (OVERDUE) label.

keyPoints.text: The whole rule is three conditions: checked out, has a due date, and the due date is before today.
keyPoints.quote: return checkedOut && dueDate != null && dueDate.isBefore(today);

keyPoints.text: Nothing is stored: overdue is derived from an explicit comparison date every time.
keyPoints.quote: Nothing is stored: overdue is derived from an explicit comparison date every time it is asked for.

keyPoints.text: The service method reuses the model rule and sorts with an explicit tie-break.
keyPoints.quote: The service method reuses the model rule and sorts with an explicit tie-break

keyPoints.text: isOverdue already returns false without a due date, so the filter needs no null guard.
keyPoints.quote: `isOverdue` already returns false for books without a due date, so the filter needs no null guard.

keyPoints.text: Without the id tie-break, equal due dates keep getAllBooks' order, which would silently change if that sort changed.
keyPoints.quote: would silently change if that method's sort changed.

keyPoints.text: Do not persist an overdue boolean: time makes it wrong without any user edit.
keyPoints.quote: Do not persist an overdue boolean: time makes it wrong without any user edit.

keyPoints.text: The CLI label uses LocalDate.now() instead of the injected Clock, so a test with a fixed clock cannot control it.
keyPoints.quote: a test that injects a fixed clock cannot control what the CLI labels as overdue.

questions.prompt: Explain how a renewal must be built as a two-record change, and what the review found about checkout's borrower lookup. What does Book.renew return, which records does the service replace and in how many commits, what stops a book-only update, what information a plain due-date replacement loses and how to keep it, and what checkout checks for the book but not the borrower, with the fix.

keyPoints.text: Book.renew returns a new Book with the next version, the same borrower and checkout date, and the new due date.
keyPoints.quote: returns a new `Book` with `nextVersion`, the same borrower and checkout date, and the new due date.

keyPoints.text: The service finds the active loan, builds a replacement Loan with the new due date, and passes both replacements to one commit.
keyPoints.quote: pass both replacements to one `commit`.

keyPoints.text: If only the book is updated, LibraryData rejects the candidate before anything is written.
keyPoints.quote: `LibraryData.java:56` rejects the candidate before anything is written.

keyPoints.text: Replacing the due date loses the earlier promise.
keyPoints.quote: Replacing the due date loses the earlier promise.

keyPoints.text: To explain extensions, retain events: old date, new date, accepted time and actor.
keyPoints.quote: retain events (old date, new date, accepted time, actor).

keyPoints.text: A typed name is not a substitute for identity.
keyPoints.quote: a typed name is not a substitute for identity.

keyPoints.text: checkOutBook checks the book's version but looks the borrower up by id alone, then copies the name into the receipt.
keyPoints.quote: checks the *book* version but looks the borrower up by id alone

keyPoints.text: Fix: accept borrowerVersion and compare it the way borrower(id, version) does.
keyPoints.quote: accept `borrowerVersion` and compare it the way `borrower(id, version)` does

questions.prompt: What changes when this library core sits behind HTTP and SQL? Describe what an HTTP route should do, what clients must not choose, which failures need distinct responses, why a disabled submit button is not idempotency, what a SQL schema must avoid to keep history and what transactions do not replace, how zero affected rows must be handled, and why FileStorage.save holds two different locks.

keyPoints.text: A route validates the request, obtains the current actor, calls a policy-aware service and translates outcomes.
keyPoints.quote: validate its request, obtain the current actor, call a policy-aware service, and translate outcomes.

keyPoints.text: Clients must not choose server-owned loan ids, accepted names or storage paths.
keyPoints.quote: Clients should not choose server-owned loan IDs, accepted names, or storage paths.

keyPoints.text: Missing data, stale versions and storage outages deserve distinct responses.
keyPoints.quote: Missing data, stale versions, and storage outages deserve distinct responses.

keyPoints.text: Disabling submit gives no durable idempotency when a checkout response is lost after commit; consider request receipts and retry keys.
keyPoints.quote: Disabling a submit button also does not provide durable idempotency when a checkout response disappears after commit

keyPoints.text: Cascading deletion could erase promised history, so deletion and archival need a deliberate schema policy.
keyPoints.quote: Cascading deletion could erase promised history

keyPoints.text: Transactions do not replace authorization or expected-version checks.
keyPoints.quote: Transactions do not replace authorization or expected-version checks.

keyPoints.text: Inspect affected-row counts and tell a missing record apart from stale context.
keyPoints.quote: Inspect affected-row counts and distinguish a missing record from stale context.

keyPoints.text: A per-path monitor serializes threads inside one JVM, and the OS file lock coordinates separate processes.
keyPoints.quote: The monitor serializes threads inside one process, and the file lock coordinates separate processes.
